points.description: Mentions sequence numbers (used to order segments or detect missing data) and acknowledgements/ACKs (confirming receipt); both must be present.
States that unacknowledged or lost segments are retransmitted, triggered by a timeout or by duplicate ACKs (either trigger is acceptable).
Mentions a checksum used to detect corruption in a segment, so corrupted data is detected/discarded rather than accepted as valid.
Mentions flow control using the receive window, i.e. the receiver advertises a window size that limits how much unacknowledged data the sender may have in flight or prevents receiver buffer overflow.

rubric.notes: Award each of the four marks only for the named mechanism; no half marks are allowed. P1 requires both sequence numbers and acknowledgements, while P2 accepts either timeout or duplicate ACKs as the retransmission trigger. Vague statements that TCP is reliable without naming the mechanism earn no marks.
